breaking_news.headline: How companies can sneak new chemicals past the FDA — and into our food and supplements
breaking_news.summary: There's a sneaky way companies add new chemicals in our food, and it is there by design, and totally legal.

breaking_news.headline: SpaceX IPO expected to set record when it goes public Friday
breaking_news.summary: SpaceX will go public on the NASDAQ Friday, likely to set a record as the most valuable IPO in history. NASDAQ is making a big play for IPOs, with new rules aimed at drawing in companies like SpaceX.

breaking_news.headline: Can smartphones help explain the drop in birth rates?
breaking_news.summary: Are smartphones causing people to have fewer children?  A provocative new working paper explores the persistent drop in birth rates since the iPhone was introduced nearly two decades ago.

breaking_news.headline: Door shuts on some immigrant entrepreneurs as U.S. restricts small-business loans
breaking_news.summary: For decades, immigrants who are legal permanent residents in the U.S. could get loans through the Small Business Administration, a core pillar of small-business lending. Not anymore.

breaking_news.headline: SpaceX IPO makes history as largest ever. Stock gains 19% on first day
breaking_news.summary: The initial public offering from the rocket and AI company raised some $75 billion, making the company one of the biggest in the world — and likely making Elon Musk a trillionaire.

breaking_news.headline: Justice Dept. approves Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery
breaking_news.summary: The decision paves the way for a proposed $111 billion merger uniting two rival studio giants — Paramount, owner of CBS, and the much larger Warner, which includes HBO and CNN.

breaking_news.headline: Paramount-Warner Brothers merger gets Justice Department approval
breaking_news.summary: The Justice Department closed its investigation into the proposed $110 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Brothers Discovery, saying it found no threat to competition or consumers.

breaking_news.headline: Kennedy Center removes Trump's name from the building
breaking_news.summary: Workers finished removing President Trump's name from the facade of the Kennedy Center early Saturday, hours after a court-ordered Friday deadline to remove references to Trump from the building.

breaking_news.headline: Norway braces for verdict in rape trial of crown princess's son Høiby
breaking_news.summary: Marius Borg Høiby will appear via video link, almost three months after his trial came to an end on 40 charges, including four counts of rape.

breaking_news.headline: Fifa to pay Somali referee Artan full World Cup fee
breaking_news.summary: Somali referee Omar Artan, who was denied entry to the United States to officiate at the World Cup, will still receive his tournament fee from Fifa in full.

breaking_news.headline: 'Boyfriend duties call,' Trudeau says after skipping Canada match to watch Perry
breaking_news.summary: Cameras caught Perry running off stage to greet the former Canadian leader with a kiss.

breaking_news.headline: Tourist train overturns and injures 17 during Cártama tapas festival
breaking_news.summary: Nobody was seriously hurt as a result of the accident in the Spanish town, local authorities say.

breaking_news.headline: Protesters clash with police ahead of G7 summit in Geneva
breaking_news.summary: Swiss police deployed a water cannon and fired tear gas to disperse anti-G7 protesters after clashes.

breaking_news.headline: Teen shot and buses torched in Manhattan after historic NBA win for Knicks
breaking_news.summary: At least 63 people were arrested in the disorder after the Knicks beat the Spurs to clinch the title.

breaking_news.headline: Swiss voters reject 10 million population cap
breaking_news.summary: Nearly 55% of participants voted against the proposal to cap population by cutting migration, results show.

breaking_news.headline: Why the US economy keeps defying the odds
breaking_news.summary: Why has the American economy continued to outperform so many of its peers, despite facing the same global shocks?

breaking_news.headline: UK and Japan agree £18bn investment deal
breaking_news.summary: Japanese firms will spend billions on UK infrastructure and offshore wind, Downing Street says.

breaking_news.headline: As more US business owners retire many are selling up to their staff
breaking_news.summary: Some six million bosses of American firms will be entering retirement between now and 2035.

breaking_news.headline: UK electric car sales target set to be weakened
breaking_news.summary: The new target hasn't yet been decided, with different numbers under consideration, the BBC understands.

breaking_news.headline: Is the convertible heading into the sunset?
breaking_news.summary: UK drivers have taken a shine to the SUV but could the fate of the convertible be reversed?
